item.title: Trump has delayed the Beijing summit. China wonders if he'll ever come to the negotiating table
item.summary: The question echoing through Beijing’s diplomatic and political circles is whether U.S. President Donald Trump will show up for a summit in Beijing that was originally supposed to take place this month. Distracted by a self-launched war in Iran and facing mounting domestic pre...

item.title: Iran targets Gulf oil infrastructure as Israel kills another regime official
item.summary: Iran struck Qatar and fired missiles at Saudi Arabia after vowing attacks on oil and gas targets throughout the Gulf on Wednesday.

item.title: Pakistan and Afghanistan announce temporary pause in fighting
item.summary: Pakistan and Afghanistan have declared a temporary pause in escalating fighting, two days after Kabul blamed Islamabad for a deadly airstrike in the Afghan capital that it said killed hundreds of people at a drug rehabilitation hospital.

item.title: Israeli airstrikes in Beirut intensify, demolishing a 10-storey building and striking bridges
item.summary: Israel stepped up airstrikes on Beirut on Wednesday, killing at least 10 people and destroying a 10-storey building near the city center in the third week of its war with Hezbollah, Lebanese authorities said.

item.title: As gas prices rise, ride-hail drivers feel especially pinched at the pump
item.summary: Gas prices worldwide have soared since the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran, and the widening war has pinched tanker traffic in the crucially important Strait of Hormuz shipping route. Ride-hail drivers, many of whom are on the road for hours a day, say they're being h...

item.title: 4-day work weeks, rationing, dressing down: How some Asian countries are coping with the Iran oil crisis
item.summary: Much of the oil produced in the Middle East is exported to Asian countries, which are now using a range of different methods to adjust to the fuel crunch caused by Iran's partial blockage of the Strait of Hormuz amid its war with the U.S. and Israel.

item.title: Top U.S. counterterrorism official Joe Kent resigns over Trump's war on Iran
item.summary: Joe Kent, the director of the National Counterterrorism Center, announced his resignation on Tuesday, saying he "cannot in good conscience" back the Trump administration's war in Iran.

item.title: Is Iran waging war with mines in the Strait of Hormuz? | About That
item.summary: Andrew Chang explains what we know about Iran's sea mine capabilities and why they can be such a destructive and difficult naval threat to remove — especially in a critical shipping route. Images provided by The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock, CAT-UXO and Getty Images

item.title: Netanyahu posts video to dispel rumours of his death after disinformation spreads online
item.summary: ​Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu posted a video of himself getting a coffee on Sunday in an apparent attempt to prove that online rumours of his death have been greatly exaggerated.

item.title: Why allies aren't leaping to Trump's aid in Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is struggling to persuade other countries to help protect commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — a development analysts say is partly the result of how he has treated allies since returning to the White House last year.
